 UFC Fight Night: Amir Albazi vs Alessandro Costa Preview & Prediction
 by Owen Liao · 20 November 2026 at 12:11 pm 
 Updated 20 November 2026 at 12:46 pm 
 Post 
 Share 
 Click here for today’s sports betting tips from our expert analysts! 
 A flyweight rematch four years in the making takes place on the UFC Qatar prelims, the declining Amir Albazi meets an in-form Alessandro Costa, a man he stopped back in 2022.

 Amir Albazi: Has “The Prince” hit his ceiling?
 Amir Albazi (17-3) has sat in the flyweight rankings for a long time, but he’s the fighter on worse form coming into this one, riding back-to-back decision losses to Brandon Moreno and Kyoji Horiguchi. He’s a grappler first and a striker second, constantly closing the distance to shoot for single legs or the body lock, though he struggles to land his takedowns. When he does get it down, he transitions well, has decent control and ground and pound, and hunts the back for the rear naked. On the feet he’s low volume and not the most accurate, waiting to counter with looping right hands.
 Alessandro Costa: As dangerous as ever
 Alessandro Costa (17-5) is looking as dangerous as ever, with finishes in each of his last three fights against Stewart Nicoll, Matt Schnell and Cody Durden. He’s a genuine dual threat, with seven knockouts and seven submissions on his record, good BJJ and a reversal threat when he’s taken down. He strikes with low volume but dangerous power, mixing calf kicks with step-in straights that close the gap into short combinations, plus nice pull counters and a wild overhand. The flip side is that he lacks head movement and swings wild in the pocket, leaving him hittable and open to counters and takedowns.
 Amir Albazi vs Alessandro Costa prediction
 This is a rematch of Costa’s UFC debut, which Albazi won by third-round TKO in 2022. Costa took that fight on short notice, and I think he took that level of fight a bit too early in his career. The version we’re seeing now is a far more complete fighter. Albazi does have the higher-level experience and the better wins, with that victory over Costa and a split decision over Kai Kara-France. He’s never been finished, and his recent losses came against a declining Moreno and top contender Horiguchi. But we don’t see much improvement or development in his game fight to fight nowadays, and he seems to have reached his ceiling.
 Costa is the more dynamic striker and the more well-rounded finisher. Albazi’s low-volume, inaccurate striking shouldn’t trouble him much, and if Albazi forces the grappling, Costa’s scrambles and reversals make him tough to hold down. The danger is Costa’s wild swinging in the pocket, which gives Albazi windows to land that looping right or shoot underneath.
 It has to be noted that Costa hasn’t beaten great competition, and his UFC losses to Steve Erceg and Alden Coria show he’s come up short on every step up. He’s a fighter who’s better with confidence, and he looked timid against Coria. Right now, though, the confidence is back. It’s a pretty even matchup, but I’ll side with the more in-form fighter.
 Prediction: Costa to win
